newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump, BTC surges.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump, BTC surges.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.94 percent on Tuesday and traders said further gains were on the cards as prices seemed to have bottomed out.
"The offer is poor and any larger purchase pushes prices up. I expect the index will rise possibly up to 1,400 points this week," said Goran Spasenic, a trader at brokerage BPH.
The SBI index rose 25.5 points to 1,338.44.
Gains were further fuelled by expectations foreign investors would return in May as banks were likely to open first custodian accounts in late April.
Foreign investment was blocked in February when the central bank said internatinal investors had to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in securities.

Traders said warehousing and shopping centre operator BTC and bank Dolenjska banka might be the best investment at the moment due to their favourable business results and BTC's future expansion plans.
BTC was the top gainer, up 6.44 percent to 14,370 tolars on market rumours the company was planning to issue global depository receipts within the next six months, traders said.
BTC said it was seeking fresh capital but added issuing GDRs was only one of several options.
Overall seven shares rose and nine fell, while 11 were untraded. Turnover jumped to 93.2 million tolars from 38.5 million.

Food company Kolinska was the most actively traded, down 3.26 percent to 2,000 tolars on volume of 18,533 shares. Traders said the fall was not seen as an indicator of any problems in the company but as a result of a lack of fresh money on the market.
Preferred shares of bank Hipotekarna Banka Brezice were the leading decliners, closing 6.85 percent lower at 3,060 on volume of 20 shares.
